text: Cryo-electron microscopy requires the protein to first be crystallized before imaging, just like X-ray crystallography.
explanation: This is false: cryo-EM instead flash-freezes the protein in vitreous (non-crystalline) ice and images individual particles directly with an electron beam, combining millions of 2D projections into a 3D reconstruction. Crystallization is specifically what X-ray crystallography requires, and avoiding it is one of cryo-EM's major advantages for large complexes and membrane proteins.
